title: The empty square (2020)
hookLine: in the pandemic, Francis prays alone in the rain in St Peter's Square
carry: we are in the same boat

cards: Evening. Rain on the stones. St Peter's Square, built to hold huge crowds, is completely empty.

The city is locked down; a virus is moving through the world, and people are dying in hospitals without their families beside them. Up the wide steps, under a canopy, one figure in white walks slowly, alone.
No crowd answers him. Cameras carry the picture into kitchens, living rooms and hospital break rooms around the world. The pope has come out to pray, for a world that can't come to him.
And the reading he chose is about a boat in a storm.

teach.h: THE STORM AND THE SLEEPING JESUS.
teach.b: The service was plain, and each piece of it was chosen. First, the reading. Mark's Gospel tells of the disciples crossing the lake at night when a great storm comes up and the waves pour into the boat.
Jesus is asleep in the stern on a cushion. They wake him, and in the Douay-Rheims they say: "Master, doth it not concern thee that we perish?"
He calms the wind, and then asks them: "Why are you fearful? have you not faith yet?" Second, what Francis heard in it.
In his homily he said the storm had shown that we are all in the same boat, fragile and disoriented, all needing each other. The storm strips away the comfortable things we use to look secure.
He didn't call the storm a punishment. He said everyone was in it.

teach.h: A CRUCIFIX AND AN ICON IN THE RAIN.
teach.b: Third, what stood beside him: a wooden crucifix from a church in Rome, which tradition says was once carried through the streets in a time of plague, out in the rain, and an icon of Mary from a Roman basilica.

teach.h: A BLESSING OVER AN EMPTY SQUARE.
teach.b: At the end he held up the Eucharist in a monstrance and gave the blessing the popes call to the city and to the world, over an empty square, to everyone watching wherever they were.
Bells rang. Sirens could be heard in the distance. A man alone in the rain, praying for people he would never meet, many of them dying alone.

how: Catholics pray for the dead at every Mass and in November especially, and the blessing Urbi et Orbi is usually given by the pope at Christmas and Easter, and on rare occasions like this one.

games.q: you're Francis. the world is locked down and the square is empty. what reading do you choose?
o: a reading about the end of the world.
the disciples in a boat in a storm, waking Jesus.
a reading about a great feast.
games.why: he chose Mark 4: the storm, the sleeping Jesus, and the question, why are you fearful?

practice: Remember the people who died in those months without a hand to hold; if you know some by name, let the names come one at a time, and if not, think of a hospital corridor at night, a nurse holding up a phone so a family can say goodbye.
If you pray, pray for them and for the nurses and doctors who stood in for families; if not, simply remember them.

wordCard.voice: Monstrance. The vessel in which Pope Francis held up the Eucharist to bless the city and the world, alone in the rain over an empty St Peter's Square.

orig.note: Latin: to the city and to the world, the name of the blessing he gave over the empty square.

carryVoice: Your line: we are in the same boat. Nobody rode out that storm alone. Rest well tonight.
